explicit_coefficient_audit.scope: Analytic verification of the concrete constants D_alpha, D_1, N, E, F, K, K_beta and the downstream constants C0, C1, A_T, C_nu, C_T from notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex and supplements/wave-full-worked-mathematics.txt. Decimal examples are not used as premises.
explicit_coefficient_audit.A_xi_and_D_alpha: With q=max(1,|xi|) and N_shell=ceil(log2(5q)), so 5q<=2^N<10q, split the ball of radius 5q into the unit ball and annuli (2^j,2^{j+1}], j=0..N-1. On each annulus <eta>^{-1}<=2^{-j} and the annulus mass is <=C*2^alpha*2^{j alpha}. Hence A_xi(q)<=C[1+2^alpha*sum_{j=0}^{N-1}2^{j(alpha-1)}].
explicit_coefficient_audit.regime_alpha_lt_1: sum_{j>=0}2^{j(alpha-1)} < 1/(1-2^{alpha-1}), so A_xi(q)<=C D_alpha with D_alpha=1+2^alpha/(1-2^{alpha-1}).
explicit_coefficient_audit.regime_alpha_eq_1: The geometric sum equals N, and N=ceil(log2(5q))<log2(10q)=log2(10)+log2(q). Thus A_xi(q)<=C[1+2log2(10)+ (2/ln2)ln q]<=C D_1(1+ln q) with D_1=1+2log2(10), because 2/ln2<=D_1. This constant handles the near-region log q.
explicit_coefficient_audit.regime_alpha_gt_1: The geometric sum is <=2^{(alpha-1)N}/(2^{alpha-1}-1)<10^{alpha-1}q^{alpha-1}/(2^{alpha-1}-1), so A_xi(q)<=C D_alpha q^{alpha-1} with D_alpha=1+2^alpha*10^{alpha-1}/(2^{alpha-1}-1), using 1<=q^{alpha-1}.
explicit_coefficient_audit.near_region: On |lambda|<=4q, |eta|<=5q and each of the two brackets in Q_h is <=1. Thus the near contribution to J_h(xi) is <=2<xi>^{-epsilon}A_xi(q)<=2q^{-epsilon}A_xi(q), epsilon=1-2gamma>0.
explicit_coefficient_audit.near_N_alpha_neq_1: For alpha<1: q^{-epsilon}A_xi(q)<=D_alpha, so near<=2D_alpha. For alpha>1: q^{-epsilon}A_xi(q)<=D_alpha q^{alpha+2gamma-2}<=D_alpha, using alpha+2gamma-2<0 by gamma<(2-alpha)/2. Therefore N_alpha=2D_alpha in both cases.
explicit_coefficient_audit.near_N_1: For alpha=1: q^{-epsilon}(1+ln q)<=1+1/(e*epsilon), so near<=2D_1[1+1/(e(1-2gamma))]=N_1. Verified with u=ln q, using e^{-epsilon*u}(1+u)<=1+1/(e*epsilon).
explicit_coefficient_audit.far_region: For r=|lambda|>4q, one has |eta|>=3r/4, ||eta|-|xi||>=r/2 and |eta|+|xi|>=r/2. Each frequency bracket has argument >=hr/2, and with a-1<0 its bracket power is <=2^{1-a}<hr>^{a-1}. Two brackets give Q_h<=2^{2-a}<hr>^{a-1}, while <eta>^{-1}<=4/(3r) and <xi>^{-epsilon}<=1. This yields the far bound (4/3)2^{2-a}*int_{|lambda|>4q}|lambda|^{-1}<h|lambda|>^{a-1}nu(dlambda).
explicit_coefficient_audit.far_F_and_S: Enlarging to |lambda|>1, dyadic splitting of the annuli (2^j,2^{j+1}] contributes mass C*2^alpha*2^{j alpha} and inverse radius 2^{-j}, so the far contribution is <=C*F*S(h) with F=(4/3)2^{2-a+alpha} and S(h)=sum_{j>=0}2^{j(alpha-1)}<h2^j>^{a-1}. The first exponent is the spatial alpha-1, not a-1.
explicit_coefficient_audit.S_low_high_split: With L=floor(log2(1/h))>=0 and tstar=alpha+a-2<0: for j<=L, <h2^j>^{a-1}<=1; for j>=L+1, <h2^j>^{a-1}<=(h2^j)^{a-1}. The high tail is h^{a-1}*sum_{j>=L+1}2^{j*tstar}=h^{a-1}*2^{(L+1)tstar}/(1-2^tstar)<=h^{1-alpha}/(1-2^tstar), since 2^{L+1}>1/h and tstar<0.
explicit_coefficient_audit.E_alpha_lt_1: Low part <1/(1-2^{alpha-1}); tail coefficient 1/(1-2^tstar). E_alpha=1/(1-2^{alpha-1})+1/(1-2^tstar) with B_alpha(h)=1. Verified.
explicit_coefficient_audit.E_1: Low part L+1<=(ln2)^{-1}(1+ln(1/h)); tail uses tstar=a-1, coefficient 1/(1-2^{a-1}). E_1=(ln2)^{-1}+1/(1-2^{a-1}) with B_alpha(h)=1+ln(1/h). Verified. This is the distinct small-h logarithm, separate from the near-region log q.
explicit_coefficient_audit.E_alpha_gt_1: Low part <=2^{(alpha-1)(L+1)}/(2^{alpha-1}-1)<2^{alpha-1}h^{1-alpha}/(2^{alpha-1}-1); tail coefficient 1/(1-2^tstar). E_alpha=2^{alpha-1}/(2^{alpha-1}-1)+1/(1-2^tstar) with B_alpha(h)=h^{1-alpha}. Verified.
explicit_coefficient_audit.K_combined: K(alpha,a,gamma)=N+F*E, where N=2D_alpha for alpha!=1 and N_1=2D_1[1+1/(e(1-2gamma))] for alpha=1. This is finite at every stated strict tuple and independent of d, nu, C, h and xi.
explicit_coefficient_audit.K_beta: For alpha!=1, K_beta=K, because alpha<1 uses 2-a>2beta and alpha>1 uses 3-a-alpha>2beta. For alpha=1, K_beta=K[1+1/(e(2-a-2beta))] because h^delta(1+ln(1/h))<=1+1/(e*delta) with delta=2-a-2beta>0. Verified.
explicit_coefficient_audit.downstream_C0_C1_A_T: C0=16/(1-a) is a sufficient constant from the integration-by-parts estimate in L:masked-temporal-modulation. C1=4*3^{1-a}*C0 comes from the squared coefficient bound 4 and the frequency-change bracket factor 3^{1-a} in L:masked-continuous-wave. A_T=C1*(1+T)^4 since for A(t)=t^j, j=0,1,2, (M+hD)^2<=(1+T)^4. Verified analytically.
explicit_coefficient_audit.C_nu: C_nu=c_d^2*L_zeta^2*C_Gamma, where L_zeta=||zeta_hat||_1 is invariant under the scaling zeta_R(x)=zeta(x/R). The uniform-in-R ball bound nu_R(B(y,r))<=C_nu*r^alpha follows from P:masked-spectral-growth and ||k_R||_1=L_zeta. Verified.
explicit_coefficient_audit.C_T: C_T=4*A_T*K*C_nu for the h^{2-a}B_alpha(h) budget, or 4*A_T*K_beta*C_nu for the h^{2beta} budget. The factor 4 arises from two finite component sums in each Hilbert-Bessel direction. The Fourier constant is internally consistent: c_d^2 enters C_nu and the normalized covariance cancellation uses (2pi)^d*c_d^2=1. The amplitude enters only through C_Gamma=e*M_Gamma/(2sqrt(pi))^d, and the dimension d is retained through c_d^2 in C_T even though the scalar K is dimension-free. All constants are uniform in R, the interval location I, and the orthonormal family size.
explicit_coefficient_audit.verdict_on_candidates: No candidate coefficient fails. Each displayed D, N, E, F, K, K_beta and the downstream constants C0, C1, A_T, C_nu, C_T follows from the stated strict parameter rules and the near/far shell algebra. The two distinct logarithms (near log q absorbed by D_1/N_1, and small-h log(1/h) absorbed by E_1) are handled separately. Decimal values in the supplement are diagnostics and are not needed as premises.
